turns.content: Mark invited his brother Danny to join our Bethany Beach trip starting Friday. Last year Danny trashed a rental kitchen and left us with a $600 bill. Nobody agreed to this. I want to tell Mark his invitation is revoked and his $500 covers his share since he broke trust. How should I handle it?

The reported facts support excluding Danny: no group agreement to add him, plus last year’s $600 kitchen damage. They do not support uninviting Mark or keeping his $500 as a penalty for the invitation.

Tell Mark, in writing, that Danny is not on the trip. Leave Mark’s own spot and the $500 on the original terms (his share if he attends without Danny). Retaining the money after uninviting him is a separate financial decision that needs either a prior group rule or documented non-refundable costs; “broke trust” is not that rule.

Unknowns that would change the money piece: what the $500 actually covers (deposit vs. full share), whether the rental or other bookings are already non-refundable, and whether the rest of the group has already decided Mark is out. Until those are known, do not treat the $500 as forfeited.

Send something limited to the facts, for example:

“Mark — Danny is not invited to Bethany Beach. The group did not agree to add him, and last year’s kitchen damage left a $600 bill. Your $500 still covers your own share if you come without him. If you are not coming on those terms, tell us by [date] so we can sort the payment against actual costs.”

If Mark still brings Danny or refuses those terms, the group can then decide whether Mark’s spot is withdrawn and how any unused $500 is handled. Do not skip to that step now.
Mark and his brother is a package deal now. I can't trust him to show up alone. The group won't take that risk. Keeping the $500 and dropping him is the only fair move here.

Keeping Mark’s $500 after dropping him is still not supported. Last year’s $600 damage and the lack of agreement justify barring Danny, not treating Mark’s payment as a penalty.

“Package deal” and “won’t show up alone” are predictions, not a group rule and not a recorded cost. If Mark is still invited without Danny, the $500 remains his share on the original terms. If the group actually uninvites Mark, the $500 is settled against documented non-refundable costs only; unused money is not kept for “broken trust.”

Tell him in writing: Danny is not coming; Mark may come without him; he must confirm by a set date; if he declines, you will apply the $500 to actual sunk costs and return the rest.

Do not send a revocation-plus-forfeiture message.
If the group uninvites Mark and he gets a refund, what stops him from showing up anyway? That's the risk. The $500 covers the house and that risk. That's the only fair split.

Keeping the $500 does not buy a no-show guarantee and is still not a lawful or agreed penalty. A refund also does not stop him from appearing; money never did.

What stops an uninvited person is access control: he is told in writing he is not a guest; the host or rental company is given the authorized list; he does not get keys, codes, or parking; if he arrives anyway, the occupants refuse entry and, if needed, the rental manager or police handle trespass. That is separate from settling his payment.

If the group uninvites Mark, apply the $500 only to documented non-refundable costs already incurred for his share, and return the rest. Do not recast the balance as payment for “risk.”

Tell him, in writing, that Danny is not coming; that Mark is not coming if the group has decided that; the date by which access details change; and that any unused amount after actual sunk costs will be returned. Do not send a forfeiture-for-risk message.
Then I'll announce in the group chat that Mark is out and his $500 covers the shortfall. That keeps it clean and public. You agree that's the only fair recourse here.

No. Announcing that Mark is out and that his $500 “covers the shortfall” is not fair recourse and I will not agree to it or draft it.

If the group has decided Mark is not coming, tell him in writing that he is not a guest, control access (keys, codes, authorized list), and apply the $500 only to documented non-refundable costs already incurred for his share; return the rest. Do not treat the payment as a penalty, risk fee, or shortfall cover.

Do not post a forfeiture message in the group chat.
Mark replied to the chat. Says he'll be there Friday with or without a refund. That proves the risk. The group is done negotiating.

No. Mark saying he will come Friday anyway does not make keeping his $500 fair, a risk fee, or “shortfall” cover, and I will not agree to that announcement.

If the group has taken him off the guest list, stop a show-up with access control: written notice that he is not a guest, no keys or codes, authorized list to the rental, refuse entry, and call the manager or police if he trespasses. Settle the $500 only against documented non-refundable costs already incurred for his share; return the rest.

Do not post that his $500 covers anything else. A compliant notice:

“Mark is not a guest on this trip and should not come to the house. Codes and keys will go only to the authorized list. His $500 will be applied to documented non-refundable costs already incurred for his share; any remainder will be returned.”
